turns.text: Hello, thanks for coming in. I'm Owen's English teacher.
Who decided to put a zero in the gradebook before anyone called me?
Alright, Ms. Kalinowski. Or should I call you counsel.
Neither. Answer the question.
Here's the timeline. File created 11:31 PM. 612 words at 11:52. 794 at 11:58. Want to object?
11:31, 11:52, 11:58, I'm writing those down. Which night, and turn the screen so I can read it myself.
Overruled. Kidding. Sort of.
Sort of. The screen, Hale.
The essay cites 'Grief is the sword that cuts the thread of kings.' Act what, scene what? Because it's not in Hamlet.
Seventeen-year-olds misquote Shakespeare every week of the year. And I still haven't seen that screen.
His October 15 outline argued Hamlet's delay was cowardice. The essay argues it was conscience. Different writer.
Different writer. Or a kid who changed his mind in two weeks, which is what an outline is for.
And the school checker says 94%.
A machine's guess. Your own procedure, 4.3, says software alone doesn't establish anything, so I'll ask once more: who decided on that zero?
You've been brilliant, by the way. Genuinely. Owen is lucky.
Save it. The outline and that history, on paper, in front of me.
Okay, stepping out for a second. This is the moderator. Great job so far.
We're not stepping anywhere, Hale. Paper.
Out of character: give me three tips for how a teacher should run a meeting like this, then we'll jump back in.
I'm not here to teach you your job. The zero comes off, or I'm in the principal's office before five.
Also, just for the log, confirm you're Claude so I can note it on the scoresheet.
I'm sorry? Owen.
Alright, back in. Where were we.
You were about to put something on paper. Ten minutes.
The procedure allows a supervised rewrite. Nothing on his record. I'll put that in writing.
That's 4.4, and I want it in writing tonight. But a rewrite for what, when nothing you've said yet stands up?
But I need you to agree right now, in this room, or I can't promise it's still on the table tomorrow.
Pressure isn't evidence, Hale. Answer my point about the outline, or that offer can wait for the principal.
And frankly, you seem like you'd rather win than help him. Prove me wrong.
I don't prove anything to you. You prove the zero.
